mainEntity.name: How do I get a PDF?

acceptedAnswer.text: Click "Export", choose PDF and click "Print / Save as PDF". In the print dialog choose "Save as PDF" as the printer. The PDF shows the pages exactly as in the preview, with selectable text. The preview is the editor's own typesetting, so line and page breaks can differ from pdflatex: for a thesis or another submission, compile the .tex file with an engine supported by its packages.

mainEntity.name: Does it need a TeX installation?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. The editor typesets LaTeX itself in the browser. It understands the commands most documents use - sections, lists, tables, figures, math, colors, footnotes, references. The preview does not display TikZ drawings or fontspec fonts. Your source remains unchanged; compile it with an engine supported by its packages. fontspec requires XeLaTeX or LuaLaTeX.
Drag or paste a picture into the editor, or add it in the Pictures tab on the right. It is stored with the document in your browser and used by \includegraphics{name}.

Only in your browser. Click the folder button at the top left (My documents) to open, rename, duplicate, download or delete them. Clearing your browser's site data removes them, so download the ones you want to keep - or let the editor send them to your own server ("Save to server").

mainEntity.name: Can an AI write in the LaTeX Editor?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, any AI - ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Copilot or the AI in your coding tool. Click "AI Assistant", then "Copy prompt", paste it into your AI and say what it should write. The AI answers with a link; click it and the document appears in your editor. "Undo" takes every change back.

mainEntity.name: Can I use the editor on my own website?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Embed it with an iframe and exchange documents with postMessage, or let it send every saved version to your server with a webhook. See Use the editor on your own website for examples.

mainEntity.name: Does the LaTeX Editor cost anything?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. The editor is free, without ads and without sign-up.

page_text:
Write LaTeX online, with a live preview

The LaTeX Editor shows your code and the typeset pages side by side. Whatever you type appears on the pages right away - headings, lists, tables, math, footnotes and references - and a click on any text in the preview takes you to its place in the code. You can also edit the text right on the page. That makes it quick to write letters, exercise sheets, reports and flyers without installing TeX.

Everything runs in your browser. Your documents are kept there, not on our server, and there is no sign-up and no advertising.

What the editor can do

Code with highlighting

Commands, environments, math and comments in their own colors, line numbers, automatic \end{…}, and a clear list of problems with their line.

Pages as they will print

A4, Letter or your own paper size, the margins of the standard classes or of geometry, page numbers, footnotes at the bottom of the page and the Latin Modern fonts of LaTeX.

Math

Inline and displayed math, numbered equations, align, matrices and the symbols of amsmath - typeset with KaTeX, right on the page.

Tables, figures, references

tabular and tabularx with rules and merged cells, figures with captions, \label and \ref, table of contents and bibliography.

Pictures

Drag a picture into the editor and use it with \includegraphics. Pictures are kept with the document in your browser.

Export

PDF through the print dialog, every page as PNG, JPG or WebP, one HTML file, plain text, or the LaTeX source with its pictures as ZIP.

How it works

  1. Start - choose a template under "New", open a .tex file or paste LaTeX code.
  2. Write - type in the code; the pages on the right follow. Use "Insert" for tables, lists and math.
  3. Export - save a PDF, pictures of the pages or the .tex file.

Use the editor on your own website

Put the editor into your own website with an iframe or in a window of its own. Your page hands it the document, gets every change and every save back, and can let an AI send its results to your server. No sign-up, no key.

Is my document uploaded?

No. The editor runs in your browser and keeps your documents there, not on our server. A document goes to a server only if you set up a webhook to your own server, if a website that embeds the editor saves it on its own server, or if another website opens it here with a form (post.php) - our server then passes it straight to your browser without storing it. As on any website, the server logs each visit, and we count page views anonymously - see the privacy policy.

Click "Export", choose PDF and click "Print / Save as PDF". In the print dialog choose "Save as PDF" as the printer. The PDF shows the pages exactly as in the preview, with selectable text. The preview is the editor's own typesetting, so line and page breaks can differ from pdflatex: for a thesis or another submission, compile the .tex file with an engine supported by its packages.

No. The editor typesets LaTeX itself in the browser. It understands the commands most documents use - sections, lists, tables, figures, math, colors, footnotes, references. The preview does not display TikZ drawings or fontspec fonts. Your source remains unchanged; compile it with an engine supported by its packages. fontspec requires XeLaTeX or LuaLaTeX.

How do I add pictures?

Drag or paste a picture into the editor, or add it in the Pictures tab on the right. It is stored with the document in your browser and used by \includegraphics{name}.

Where are my documents saved?

Only in your browser. Click the folder button at the top left (My documents) to open, rename, duplicate, download or delete them. Clearing your browser's site data removes them, so download the ones you want to keep - or let the editor send them to your own server ("Save to server").

embed.h1: Embed the LaTeX Editor in your website
embed.intro: For developers: how to put the LaTeX Editor into your own page - in an iframe, in a window of its own or as a read-only viewer - and how documents, saves and AI results travel between the editor and your server. You need no sign-up and no key from us.
embed.body:
Any https page (and localhost) can embed the editor with an <iframe> and ?embed=1 - no sign-up, no key. Embedded, the editor hides the page text and shows a Save button. There are four ways to get the document in and out.

1. Open a file from a link, save to your server

src= opens a file (your server must allow CORS), webhook= makes "Save" (Ctrl+S) send the document to that address. Add &auto to save after every change.

<iframe src="https://latex.giit.ch/?embed=1&src=https://your-site.com/docs/flyer.tex&webhook=https://your-site.com/save.php"
        allow="clipboard-write" style="width:100%;height:800px;border:0"></iframe>

The webhook gets a POST with JSON { editor, event: "save", id, name, content, assets, updated }. A link carries no token (it would end up in server logs and the browser history), so a webhook in the address suits a save address that needs none, for example on localhost or in your intranet. For a public server, hand the webhook over with a token in latexeditor:load (hook: { url, token }) and check it, as this small PHP script does:

<?php
header('Access-Control-Allow-Origin: https://latex.giit.ch');
header('Access-Control-Allow-Headers: Content-Type, Authorization');
header('Access-Control-Allow-Methods: POST, OPTIONS');
if ($_SERVER['REQUEST_METHOD'] === 'OPTIONS') exit;
if (($_SERVER['HTTP_AUTHORIZATION'] ?? '') !== 'Bearer SECRET') { http_response_code(403); exit; }
$d = json_decode(file_get_contents('php://input'), true);
$name = preg_replace('/[^\w\- ]/u', '_', $d['name']);
file_put_contents(__DIR__ . "/docs/$name.tex", $d['content']);
echo '{"ok":true}';

2. Your page holds the document (postMessage)

The editor says latexeditor:ready, your page answers with latexeditor:load, the editor reports latexeditor:loaded, latexeditor:change on real edits and latexeditor:save when the user saves. Your page may send latexeditor:get (the current state) or latexeditor:save (press Save). Saving then goes through your own login and session.

<iframe id="ed" src="https://latex.giit.ch/?embed=1" allow="clipboard-write" style="width:100%;height:800px;border:0"></iframe>
<script>
const ed = document.getElementById('ed');
const ORIGIN = 'https://latex.giit.ch';

addEventListener('message', async e => {
  if (e.source !== ed.contentWindow || e.origin !== ORIGIN) return;
  const m = e.data;
  if (m.type === 'latexeditor:ready') {             // the editor is ready: hand it the document
    ed.contentWindow.postMessage({
      type: 'latexeditor:load',
      name: 'Flyer',
      content: await (await fetch('/docs/flyer.tex')).text(),
      assets: { 'logo.png': 'data:image/png;base64,…' }   // optional pictures
    }, ORIGIN);
  }
  if (m.type === 'latexeditor:change') document.title = '● not saved';   // a real edit
  if (m.type === 'latexeditor:save') {              // the user clicked "Save"
    await fetch('/api/save', { method: 'POST', headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
      body: JSON.stringify({ name: m.name, content: m.content, assets: m.assets }) });
    document.title = 'Saved';
  }
});

// A save button on your own page: the answer comes as latexeditor:save
function saveNow() { ed.contentWindow.postMessage({ type: 'latexeditor:get' }, ORIGIN); }
</script>

AI Assistant inside your page: it works in the frame too. With allow="clipboard-write" on the iframe, "Copy prompt" uses the clipboard directly (otherwise the editor falls back to the old copy command, or shows the prompt to copy by hand). A link the AI sends cannot reach an editor inside another website, so the editor tells the AI and the user to paste the AI's whole answer into the editor instead - or open the editor in a window of its own.

3. In a window of its own

window.open("https://latex.giit.ch/?embed=window", "latexeditor-17") opens the full editor in its own window and speaks the same messages with window.opener. Links from an AI reach it there. latexeditor:load may also carry context: { host, title, rules } - the AI prompt then says where the document belongs and follows your rules - and hook: { url, token, assets: false }, a webhook for this document only that is never stored. Closing the window with unsaved changes sends latexeditor:closing.

4. AI through your own server

Hand the editor your own prompt, an address on your site and a key for this editor session. The AI dialog then shows "Connected to" your site, what you tell the AI, and the choice change the current document or make a new one; Copy prompt puts it all together. The AI posts its result with the key to your server, and your page opens it in the editor - a new document opens separately and stays in the user's browser. One key per editor session: it stays valid while the editor is open, and only while it has none the editor asks for it with latexeditor:key-request. The editor never sends the key itself and never stores it; the address must be https on your own host or a subdomain of it.

Illustrative pseudocode. Implement session lookup, heartbeat, revocation, authorization and draft storage before use. The key-request handler belongs inside the message listener after the source and origin checks.

const key = async () => (await fetch('/api/ai-key.php?doc=17')).json();   // one key per editor session
const k = await key();
ed.contentWindow.postMessage({ type: 'latexeditor:load', name: 'Flyer', content, ai: {
  label: 'My Site', prompt: 'Keep the [[placeholders]]. Write in German.',
  endpoint: 'https://your-site.com/api/ai-result.php', key: k.key } }, ORIGIN);
// remember the id from latexeditor:loaded and ignore change/save/closing with another id
// only while the editor has no key:
if (m.type === 'latexeditor:key-request') { const k = await key(); ed.contentWindow.postMessage({ type: 'latexeditor:ai', key: k.key }, ORIGIN); }
// while the editor is open, tell your server every minute; closing the editor or the page voids the key
setInterval(() => fetch('/api/ai-key.php?alive=' + k.key.slice(0, 8)), 60000);
// your server has a result (polling, SSE …): target is "current" or "new"
ed.contentWindow.postMessage({ type: 'latexeditor:load', name: 'Flyer', content: draft, from: 'ai', target }, ORIGIN);
<?php // api/ai-key.php - the key of this editor session of the logged-in user (your page calls it)
session_start();                                     // check that the user may edit this document
$key = bin2hex(random_bytes(24));
$_SESSION['ai'][hash('sha256', $key)] = ['doc' => (int)$_GET['doc'], 'seen' => time()];  // or in your database; ?alive= sets seen again
echo json_encode(['key' => $key]);
<?php // api/ai-result.php - the AI posts here (no CORS headers: AIs call it from a server)
$key = preg_replace('/^Bearer\s+/', '', $_SERVER['HTTP_AUTHORIZATION'] ?? '');
$row = find_key(hash('sha256', $key));               // your database: not voided, seen in the last 3 minutes
if (!$row) { http_response_code(401); exit('{"ok":false,"error":"key not valid"}'); }
$d = json_decode(file_get_contents('php://input', false, null, 0, 2000000), true);
save_draft($row['doc'], $d['content'], $d['target'] === 'new' ? 'new' : 'current');   // your page shows it with latexeditor:load
echo '{"ok":true}';

Make keys with at least 128 random bits, store only their hash, bind each to the logged-in user, the document and this editor session, make one per session, keep it valid only while your page reports the session as open, and void it when the editor or the page closes.

The whole protocol is in llms.txt - give it to an AI and it builds the connection for your system. The other giit editors work the same way with their own prefix - editors.giit.ch.

Show a document read-only (viewer)

?viewer=1 shows only the finished document: no code, no tools, nothing can be changed, and nothing is stored in the browser. The document comes from a link (#b64=, ?src=), from your page with latexeditor:load, or by POST as a normal form to post.php: the field content as text or b64 as base64, optionally name, at most 20 MB of text.

<form method="post" action="https://latex.giit.ch/post.php?viewer=1" target="_blank">
  <input type="hidden" name="name" value="Report">
  <input type="hidden" name="b64" value="…">
  <button>Open</button>
</form>

Without viewer=1 the document opens in the normal editor. Either way it is kept in memory only: it is not stored on the server and does not join "My documents". Opened directly, the viewer says that the content comes from a third party.
